result.topic_en: In Latin, Riemann transforms a quadratic differential form into polar or Euclidean form ($dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$) and treats the special case $\kappa_1=0$, where the coordinate curves cannot be real; he notes the remaining cases are not yet solved.

methods.what: Change of variables to cylindrical (polar) coordinates, giving the Euclidean metric
Complex substitution transforming the form into $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$
Elimination of $\gamma$ to give the equations of the coordinate curves

items.quote: Sed aequationes, ex his eliminando $\gamma$ prodeuntes, scilicet ... curvas reales repraesentare nequeunt.
items.english: But the equations obtained from these by eliminating $\gamma$, namely ..., cannot represent real curves.

items.quote: In casibus reliquis quaestionem plano persolvere nondum contigit.
items.english: In the remaining cases it has not yet been possible to solve the question completely.
